BAR for rust-1 (written 2026-10-03 before any run). This is a BAR: it can come out against Rust, for Rust, or as a tie. Expected values are written below so a surprise is visible.

 RULE A AND HOSTS (verifier pass 2026-10-03; applies to every label in this bar). LOG.md 2026-09-12 14:16Z ruled box2 timing numbers INADMISSIBLE (Rule A: timing numbers only on box1; a second CPU class needs a third machine) and state/BOXES.md still reads, for box1, "NO timing numbers until CPUQuota/thermal checked" and, for box2, "NO timing numbers (Rule A)". box3 is the same CPU as box2 (N4020) and does not supply a second class. Therefore the ONLY labelled host is box1; box2 and box3 are REPORTED with no label ("informal per Rule A"). RESEARCH_LOOP.md E6 treated a quiet box1 as Rule-A legal timing iron. Before registration the registrar must (1) check box1 for CPUQuota and thermal state while idle and record the dated result in the ledger ref, and (2) get the BOXES.md box1 line updated. Spot read only, not the check: ssh cm-box1 at 2026-10-04 00:12Z showed cm-tick CPUQuotaPerSecUSec=infinity, thermal zones 25.0, 27.8 and 29.8 C, 2095 MHz at load average 1.68 (other jobs running). A written Fable or Justin ruling that supersedes the 2026-09-12 ruling and admits box2 may reinstate box2 as a labelled host by amend-bar before start, never after; the original two-host rules are kept below in brackets for that case.

ANSWERS (three separate answers, never merged into one verdict, never written as "Rust wins" or "Rust loses" without the qualifier):
 IMPLEMENTATION   = arm L: our CIS-2 implementation in Rust (cis2_ref) versus our CIS-2 implementation in C (verify3 / sv5_driver), same compiler effort. These are two independent implementations of one specification (different tokenizer, KV-cache layout, loader and allocator), not one algorithm written in two languages. The language effect alone is separated only by rust-5 (same loop in both languages). Nothing in this bar is a language verdict.
 FRAMEWORK  = arm G versus PyTorch versus llama.cpp: a Rust program calling a library kernel, against two non-Rust stacks. Each arm is named pure Rust or not (see below).
 KERNELS    = arm X (optional): our own fast Rust kernels against the library kernels inside torch (MKL). Not a statement about the Rust language.

QUESTION. On the same small model and the same 64 teacher-forced tokens on an old laptop CPU, is our Rust implementation of CIS-2 (cis2_ref) faster, level or slower than our C implementation (verify3) (implementation against implementation, not language alone), how do a Rust program calling a library kernel, PyTorch and llama.cpp compare (framework), and how much memory does each use?

WHAT IS COMPARED (all on SmolLM2-135M, one weights file per format, sha256 recorded before the initial timing run).
 L-R  Rust-fixed: cis2_ref, fixed-order scalar fp32, no-hash plain-generation mode (small patch if missing; the patch is written before any timing, limited to switching off hashing and receipt output with no change to the decode loop, by one author in one session, and its diff sha256 and line count are recorded and frozen with the other flags; the same is done for L-C, and unequal patch size is stated in the result). NOT PURE RUST: cis2-spec Cargo.toml enables tokenizers with features = ["onig"] and Cargo.lock lists onig and onig_sys (C Oniguruma; read 2026-10-04). The rust-2b rule (cargo tree --edges normal,build, any -sys crate, build.rs that invokes a C compiler) is run on L-R before timing and its output kept; a pure-Rust tokenizer build would change the program and is not made. Cargo.lock package count recorded (104 today).
 L-C  C-fixed: verify3 / sv5_driver, same algorithm, no-hash plain-generation mode. C11, libc and libm only.
 G-OB Rust glue + OpenBLAS: the cis2_ref decode loop with each matrix-vector product replaced by cblas_sgemv (openblas-src, system OpenBLAS, version and core type recorded, OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1). NOT pure Rust (links a C/Fortran library). Arithmetic differs from L-R and L-C (vectorised across k, may fuse), so no digest is required; the largest logit difference to L-C on the 64 positions is reported.
 G-MKL (optional) Rust glue + MKL: same, calling cblas_sgemv from libmkl_rt (pip "mkl" wheel, version recorded, MKL_VERBOSE output kept). NOT pure Rust. If G-MKL is absent, the FRAMEWORK sentence says "Rust glue + OpenBLAS versus PyTorch + MKL: kernels differ, so this is stack against stack, not glue alone". G-MKL is required for any FRAMEWORK sentence that claims "glue alone"; without G-MKL that wording is not written. G-OB is the required arm; G-MKL is optional.
 T    PyTorch: torch 2.14.0+cpu wheel (the wheel used in cap-1b), fp32, manual forward loop with KV cache fed the fixed token ids (no generate()), torch.inference_mode(), no torch.compile, attention implementation sdpa, torch.set_num_threads(N), torch.set_num_interop_threads(1), OMP_NUM_THREADS=N, MKL_NUM_THREADS=N; torch.__config__.show() output (MKL or OpenBLAS state) and MKL_VERBOSE kept; on the N4020 hosts the dispatch line is recorded. transformers version copied from SV5B and written in the result. NOT pure Rust (Python plus C++ plus MKL).
 Q    llama.cpp: one commit pinned (b11381 or newer, hash recorded), built with the host's own flags, F32 GGUF made from the same safetensors, one-token-at-a-time decode over the fixed ids through the llama.cpp API (a small C++ driver), -ngl 0, threads N. Q8_0 GGUF is an extra row, labelled "different arithmetic". NOT pure Rust (C/C++).
 X    (optional) Rust-fast: a Rust engine with AVX2 kernels and scalar fallback on the same architecture. Counts only if built and verified by 2026-10-08. If it is not built the result reads "engine: NOT TESTED" and no verdict of any kind is written for it.
 Extra, reported only, no label: Candle CPU (NOT pure Rust: default matmul is the Rust gemm crate, optional MKL off, version recorded).
 Not run, known: torch on box4 and box5 ("Illegal instruction" on import, R/2026-10-01-SW0-CPU-TRAIN-THROUGHPUT.md). 360M is not in this bar (verify3 stops on non-pinned weights and no digest reference exists); a 360M extension needs its own bar written beforehand.

SAME WORK. Prompts: the leading 8 of the sv-5 prompt set (file path and sha256 recorded at build). The 64 token ids per prompt are the greedy output of L-C, produced once, stored with sha256, with no EOS stop. Every arm decodes exactly those ids (teacher-forced), so sequence lengths are equal by construction. One extra warm-up prompt is run beforehand and discarded. Weights: L-R and L-C read the bf16 file and widen to fp32 (the pinned format); T, Q and G read the fp32 conversion of the same bf16 values (identical numbers, different load path; stated in the result).

FIXED SETTINGS TO RECORD (and freeze before the initial timing). Rust: rustc version, RUSTFLAGS, opt-level, lto fat, codegen-units 1, panic abort, target x86-64 baseline gnu (a musl static build is a separate extra, reported only, and is the only form built for box4 and box5), global allocator, whether rayon is linked and the pool size (1 at N=1, checked by Threads). C: gcc version, -O2 and -O3 each built, -mno-fma -ffp-contract=off, no -ffast-math; clang as an extra. Per host the "C reference" is the faster of the two C builds and the "Rust reference" is the faster of Rust opt-level 2 and 3 (rule fixed now, applied mechanically to the medians). Both languages get the same effort: neither source is tuned after the initial timing run.

METRIC AND STATISTIC. Timing is the in-process wall of decode steps 2 to 64 (63 steps) per prompt. Per-rep value = (8 x 63 tokens) divided by the sum of the 8 prompt walls, in tokens per second. Statistic = median of 5 per-rep values per arm per host (10 when a label is INCONCLUSIVE, once). Threads N=1 for every label; N=2 on box1 and box2 is reported with no label. Memory: peak PSS and peak anonymous bytes sampled every 50 ms from /proc/<pid>/smaps_rollup over the whole process, plus VmHWM; the values used are the medians of the 5 per-rep peaks of PSS and of anonymous bytes. The Rust safetensors crate maps the weights file (mmap) and the C loader read()s it, so PSS carries an I/O-method effect; the result states the load method of each arm. Reported with no label: prefill tokens per second, load time, time from process start to the opening generated token with warm page cache (cold cache belongs to rust-4).

HYGIENE. Host idle (uptime load average below 0.3 and fx status clear before and after, else the rep is void); no CPUQuota; every job under systemd-run --user with MemoryMax box1 4.5 GB, box2 and box3 2.8 GB, box4 and box5 80 percent of the free -m total (a job killed by the limit is recorded as OOM, not dropped); CPU MHz from /proc/cpuinfo before and after each rep, a rep with more than 15 percent drop is discarded and repeated (three discards on one host make that host INVALID); arm order rotated each rep; thread count checked from /proc/<pid>/status. penguin is never used for timing.

LABELS FOR EVERY OUTCOME (no gaps, no overlaps).
 Band S (implementation arm and any same-algorithm pair). r = Rust median speed / C median speed. RUST AHEAD: r > 1.05 and every Rust rep value is above every C rep value. TIE: 0.95 <= r <= 1.05 (both boundaries are TIE). RUST BEHIND: r < 0.95 and every C rep value is above every Rust rep value. INCONCLUSIVE: r outside 0.95 to 1.05 but the rep ranges overlap; the reps are redone once as 10; if the ranges still overlap the label is TIE (NOT SEPARABLE).
 Band W (cross-stack pairs: G vs T, G vs Q, X vs T). r = left arm median speed / second arm median speed. LEFT ARM AHEAD: r > 1.10 and non-overlapping reps. TIE: 0.90 <= r <= 1.10. LEFT ARM BEHIND: r < 0.90 and non-overlapping reps. Overlap outside the band: INCONCLUSIVE, redone as 10, then TIE (NOT SEPARABLE).
 Labels are given for the labelled host box1 only (Rule A above); box2 and box3 lines are reported with no label:
  IMPLEMENTATION speed: Band S, L-R against L-C, per host. Overall label = the box1 label (IMPLEMENTATION: RUST AHEAD, RUST BEHIND, or LEVEL for TIE and NOT SEPARABLE); if box1 is INVALID there is no overall label and none is built from box2 or box3. [Only if a Rule A ruling admitting box2 is recorded and the bar amended before start: over the two bar hosts both AHEAD gives RUST AHEAD, both BEHIND gives RUST BEHIND, both TIE (or NOT SEPARABLE) gives LEVEL, any other pair gives IMPLEMENTATION: MIXED (both host labels quoted), and one INVALID host gives no overall label.]
  IMPLEMENTATION memory: m = L-R peak PSS / L-C peak PSS. RUST LOWER: m < 0.95 and every L-R rep peak below every L-C rep peak. TIE: 0.95 <= m <= 1.05. RUST HIGHER: m > 1.05 and every L-R rep peak above every L-C rep peak. Overlap outside the band: INCONCLUSIVE then TIE (NOT SEPARABLE) after 10 reps. The label is computed on peak PSS and, separately, on peak anonymous bytes; if the two labels differ the line reads IMPLEMENTATION (memory): MIXED (PSS <label>, anonymous <label>), because of the mmap against read() difference. Combined over hosts by the same rule as speed (box1 only while Rule A stands).
  FRAMEWORK speed: Band W for G-OB against T, G-OB against Q, and (if built) G-MKL against T, per host. Reported, no combination across pairs. FRAMEWORK memory: peak PSS of G, T, Q, L-R and L-C shown side by side with ratios, no label (different load paths).
  KERNELS (arm X only): Band W for X against T on box1 (box2 reported). If X is absent: "engine: NOT TESTED". X against Q is reported as a ratio with no label (expected behind).

TRUST COLUMN (reported next to every speed line). (1) L-R and L-C: the full-logit digest of the 64-token stream must be equal to each other (reference = the L-C output) and equal across all hosts they ran on, and equal across the 5 reps. (2) T: hidden-state hash equal across box1 and the Celeron hosts, expected NO (200 of 200 clean runs differ, tokens equal; R/2026-10-02-SV5-EXACT-REPLAY-VS-TOPLOC-VS-RERUN-R2.md finding 3; SV5B gives only the seconds per prompt and 0 of 200 token differences, no hash row), reported and not argued. (3) dependency count per arm (Cargo.lock packages, pip packages, build-time libraries). (4) lines of the decode loop per arm.

EXPECTED VALUES (ESTIMATE, written before any run; a result far from these is flagged SURPRISE in the result sentence).
 IMPLEMENTATION speed: TIE about 65 percent, RUST BEHIND about 20 percent, RUST AHEAD about 15 percent. Both arms are one strict left-to-right add chain per output with no FMA, so the ratio should sit near 1.0 by construction (CRITIC claim 2, not benchmarked). Level of the numbers: C-fixed verify3 on box1 ran 0.63 tokens/s before the KV-cache fix and 3.6 tokens/s after it (5.7x, LOG.md 2026-09-23 21:07; a different prompt set, not a labelled measurement), so L-C and L-R are expected at about 1 to 3.6 tokens/s on box1 (ESTIMATE; the low end is a guess for Rust) and about 3 times lower on box2 and box3 (torch seconds per prompt, box2 68.6 against box1 23.7, SV5B).
 WALL CLOCK AND COST CAP (ESTIMATE). One arm-rep decodes 8 prompts x 63 timed tokens plus prefill, about 600 token-equivalents. Strict arms (Rust O2 and O3, C O2 and O3, 4 builds) x 5 reps: box1 about 1 h at 3.6 tokens/s and about 3.3 h at 1 token/s; library arms (G-OB, G-MKL, T, Q at about 10 tokens/s) about 20 min; box1 total about 1.3 to 3.7 h, up to double with the 10-rep redo; box2 and box3 about 3 times longer each. Registered cost cap: 0 USD, wall cap 8 box-hours on box1, 24 box-hours on each of box2 and box3, 12 box-hours on each of box4 and box5; an arm that would exceed its cap is stopped, recorded COST-CAPPED and gets no label.
 IMPLEMENTATION memory: TIE about 70 percent (both widen bf16 to fp32, about 0.55 GB of weights plus caches).
 FRAMEWORK: torch rerun was about 10.8 tokens/s on box1 and 3.7 on box2 over 256 tokens including prefill (23.7 s and 68.6 s per prompt, R/2026-10-02-SV5B-LONG-OUTPUT-RERUN.md); expect T above G-OB on box1 (and on box2, reported) (G-OB BEHIND about 55 percent, TIE about 30 percent, AHEAD about 15 percent), and Q above G-OB (llama.cpp F32 about 1.5 to 3 times faster than the strict-order arms). Torch memory above the strict arms (Python and MKL runtime on top of 0.55 GB).
 KERNELS: X, if built, BEHIND T about 60 percent (three Rust AVX2 rewrites already lost to our own kernel, R/2026-09-07-KERNEL-V4-V5-NEGATIVE.md).

INVALID (the affected label gets no verdict, and the run is redone): host load 0.3 or more; a kept rep with clock drop above 15 percent; different weights, prompts, token ids or thread counts between the two arms of a pair; an arm of a pair not run on the labelled host box1 (that pair only); a patch diff hash for L-R or L-C that changed after the initial timing; L-R and L-C digests differ (a correctness finding is recorded and the implementation labels are INVALID until the cause is found); a harness bug in one arm; Threads in /proc not equal to N; the L-C 64-id file hash changed after initial use.

FIXED NOW (may not change after the initial timing run): the arms, the pair definitions, the prompts, 64 tokens, teacher forcing from the L-C output, steps 2 to 64 as the timed window, the per-rep unit, 5 reps and the single redo as 10, bands S and W and their boundaries, the faster-of-two-opt-levels rule, the flags listed above (their recorded values are frozen at the initial timing), N=1 for labels, labelled host box1 (box2 and box3 reported, Rule A), memory limits, and the sentences below. Allowed to change before the initial timing run only, by amend-bar with a reason: versions and hashes not yet known.

HOSTS. Labelled host: box1 (i5-5200U, AVX2). Reported hosts, no label (Rule A): box2 (Celeron N4020, no AVX2), box3 (same CPU as box2, torch runs), box4 (Sempron SI-42, SSE3) and box5 (Pentium T2310, SSSE3), the last two with L-R (static musl cross-build, built on penguin) and L-C only. Penguin: controller, builds, no timing.

SENTENCES (exactly one per outcome; every sentence names which of the three answers it is about).
 IMPLEMENTATION speed: "IMPLEMENTATION (our CIS-2 implementation in Rust, cis2_ref, against our CIS-2 implementation in C, verify3; two independent implementations, same compiler effort, SmolLM2-135M decode, N=1): on <host> the Rust implementation is <ahead of | level with | behind | level with (not separable from)> the C implementation, speed ratio r=<x> over <5|10> reps. Tokenizer, KV layout, loader and allocator differ, so this is not a language verdict; the language effect alone is separated only by rust-5." Overall line: "IMPLEMENTATION: <RUST AHEAD | RUST BEHIND | LEVEL | MIXED (box1 <label>, box2 <label>)>."
 IMPLEMENTATION memory: "IMPLEMENTATION (memory): Rust peak PSS is <lower than | level with | higher than> C on <host>, m=<x>; peak anonymous bytes <lower than | level with | higher than>, m=<y>; load methods differ (mmap, read())."
 FRAMEWORK: "FRAMEWORK (stack against stack, not language): <arm> is <ahead of | level with | behind> <PyTorch fp32 + MKL | llama.cpp F32> on <host>, r=<x>. Kernels differ unless G-MKL was used. <arm> is <pure Rust | not pure Rust>."
 KERNELS: "KERNELS (our Rust kernels against MKL inside torch): the Rust-fast engine is <ahead of | level with | behind> torch on <host>, r=<x>. This is a statement about our kernels." If not built: "engine: NOT TESTED."
 Headline sentence (always the same form): "implementation: <label>; framework: <label per pair>; engine: <label | NOT TESTED>." No sentence of the form "Rust speed win" or "Rust is not a speed win" is written; no sentence about Rust against PyTorch speed is written unless the FRAMEWORK form above is used.
host: box1 (labelled); box2,box3 reported; box4,box5 Rust and C only
title: rust-1: decode speed and memory on SmolLM2-135M: our Rust vs our C CIS-2 (IMPLEMENTATION), Rust+OpenBLAS vs PyTorch vs llama.cpp (FRAMEWORK), optional Rust engine (KERNELS)

None of the nine items moves a boundary, a band, a statistic, a host role, a cap, an expected value or a label.
 R1 Load. "uptime load average below 0.3 and fx status clear before and after" is read as: at the start of every arm run the 1-minute load average is below 0.3 and no other leg-* or sv5-* user unit is active and no llama-bench or ggml-rpc-server process is alive (the runner waits up to 10 minutes; if the host does not settle the rep is void and repeated); at the end of the run no other such unit is active; the load average at the end is recorded in every row and is not gated, because one single-thread arm run leaves the 1-minute load average near 1.0, so a gate on it would void every rep. In place of an idle test after the run, the runner measures the other load during the run itself: it reads the busy CPU time per logical CPU from /proc/stat (user, nice, system, irq, softirq and steal, in seconds) before the arm process starts and after it ends, and subtracts the arm process's own CPU time (utime plus stime of the reaped child) and the runner's own process CPU time. The two figures of a rep are (a) that remainder on the arm's CPU and on its hyper-threading sibling(s), together, as a fraction of the arm process's wall time, and (b) the same remainder over all logical CPUs of the host, in CPUs averaged over the arm process's wall time. The void limits are relative to an idle baseline measured in the job. After the idle gate has passed and before rep 0 (nothing timed yet, no arm running), the runner measures the baseline with the same foreign-load formula it uses for a rep: 6 windows of 20 s each. The baseline is the maximum over the 6 windows, separately for (a) and for (b). The limits are the baseline plus a margin, 2 percentage points for (a) and 0.05 CPU for (b), and never below 2 percent for (a) and 0.10 CPU for (b). A rep is void, recorded as VOID and repeated, when its figure (a) is above limit (a) or its figure (b) is above limit (b). If the baseline itself is above 15 percent for (a) or above 0.30 CPU for (b), the job ends INVALID with the reason host_not_idle and nothing is timed. The baseline (all 6 windows and the two maxima), the margins, the floors and the resulting limits are printed in the RESULT line and are carried in every row, next to the two figures of the rep; the margins, the floors and the baseline rule are fixed by this amendment, and no rep is excluded after the fact for any other load. Voids from this rule and from the idle test are counted together; more than 6 voids in one job stop the job as PARTIAL.

"CPU MHz from /proc/cpuinfo before and after each rep, a rep with more than 15 percent drop is discarded" is read as: the reading is the MHz of the CPU the arm is pinned to (R6), taken from /proc/cpuinfo once a second from 2 s after the start of the arm process to its end. The reference is the median of the per-rep medians of the kept reps of that host so far (all arms); for the opening rep of a host it is that rep's own median. A rep is discarded and repeated when its lowest reading or its median is more than 15 percent below the reference, or when a thermal-throttle counter of the host changed during it (counters exist where the kernel exposes thermal_throttle in sysfs; the clock rule alone applies elsewhere). The third discard on a host makes the host INVALID, as the bar says. The reference is not the highest MHz seen anywhere in the job: on hosts with the schedutil governor and turbo (box2, box3) idle readings change by more than 15 percent within seconds, so such a reference would void the host by construction.
